scope: Owner-scoped unadmitted URI metadata staging through the shared local command path

includes: Core bounds, owner guard, rollback, generation exhaustion and state preservation
Strict source-result projection and generation-zero query distinction
Actual OwnerClient staging, two-client sharing, exact replay, clear and restart fences
Actual CLI replay, checkpoint privacy, clear and crash recovery
Actual Rust FFI byte replay without playback activation

verified: Both methods use schema version one and the existing command envelope.
Staging requires the current owner and revision; a named session must remain current.
The shared summary returns only owner-scoped staged identity, generation, unadmitted status and byte counts.
The retained URI and metadata capacities stay within 8192 and 65536 bytes respectively.
Empty URI and metadata clear staging; successful mutations have positive generations.
Initial or restored queries allow generation zero and no descriptor.
Exact retained replay returns the original receipt after a later replacement without altering the new descriptor.
Checkpoints and general state/event snapshots exclude raw URI, metadata and staging.
Staging preserves local playback, queue, epochs, gain, mute and consent.
A failed transaction or exhausted generation preserves the prior descriptor.
limits: No network source is admitted or advertised by these methods.
No listener, URL fetch, decoder, playback takeover, output selection, consent or Unmute occurs.
This metadata foundation does not qualify T14 or UPnP interoperability.
Rust FFI is tested; new Swift and Kotlin source-method scenarios remain unqualified.
Current Mac and GUI native qualification do not transfer from earlier source snapshots.
Exact replay remains bounded by the existing shared receipt retention policy.
